title: Organisation of an ecosystem
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.7.2-c03 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.7.2.2-xt1 term and clue written for the game; 4.7.2-c02 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.7.2.2-xt2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: 4.7.2-q01, 4.7.2-q06, 4.7.2-q08, 4.7.2-q02, 4.7.2-q07, 4.7.2-q09, 4.7.2-q03, 4.7.2-x01 (written for the game), 4.7.2-q10, 4.7.2-q04, 4.7.2-q05, 4.7.2-q11.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Precipitation
items.clue: Water falling from clouds as rain, snow, sleet or hail

items.label: Food chain
items.clue: A way of representing feeding relationships within a community.

items.label: Evaporation
items.clue: Liquid water turning into vapour, for example from the surface of the sea

questions.stem: How does the producer at the start of a food chain obtain its biomass?

options.text: By taking in ready-made food from soil
By feeding on other living organisms
By using photosynthesis to make glucose
By absorbing ready-made food in water

questions.explanation: Photosynthetic organisms are the producers of biomass for life on Earth: the producer is usually a green plant or alga which makes glucose by photosynthesis.

questions.stem: What is the role of microorganisms in cycling materials through an ecosystem?

options.text: They take in carbon dioxide from the air and ions from soil
They return carbon dioxide to the air and ions to the soil
They remove carbon dioxide and mineral ions from this cycle
They lock carbon dioxide and mineral ions in the dead matter

questions.explanation: Microorganisms cycle materials by returning carbon to the atmosphere as carbon dioxide, to be used by plants in photosynthesis, and mineral ions to the soil.

questions.stem: A gardener wants rapid decay of waste plant material in a compost heap, to use the compost as a natural fertiliser. Which conditions give the fastest rate of decay?

options.text: Very hot, dry, with oxygen present
Warm, moist and with oxygen present
Warm, moist and with oxygen kept out
Warm, dry and with oxygen present

questions.explanation: Temperature, water and the availability of oxygen affect the rate of decay, so gardeners provide optimum conditions: warm, moist and with oxygen available.

questions.stem: In the food chain lettuce → slug → hedgehog → fox, the hedgehog is:

options.text: a secondary consumer in the chain
a tertiary consumer in the chain
a primary consumer in the chain
a producer of biomass in the chain

questions.explanation: Producers are eaten by primary consumers, which in turn may be eaten by secondary consumers: the hedgehog eats the slug, which is the primary consumer.

questions.stem: Which statement describes how the water cycle provides fresh water for plants and animals on land?

options.text: Salt water drains from the seas onto the land
Water used up by organisms is lost from the land
Water is continuously evaporated and precipitated
Water is lost to the seas and is not returned

questions.explanation: The water cycle provides fresh water for plants and animals on land before draining into the seas, because water is continuously evaporated and precipitated.

questions.stem: In an investigation the mass of leaf litter in a tray fell from 60 g to 24 g in 12 days. What was the mean rate of decay?

options.text: 3.0 g per day
2.0 g per day
5.0 g per day
36.0 g per day

questions.explanation: The rate change in decay is the change in mass divided by the time taken: 60 g minus 24 g is 36 g, and 36 g divided by 12 days is 3.0 g per day.

questions.stem: A graph for a stable community shows that each peak in the number of lynx comes about a year after a peak in the number of hares. What does the graph show?

options.text: Predator numbers peak before prey numbers
Predator numbers peak with the prey numbers
Predator numbers stay level as prey cycle
Predator numbers peak after prey numbers

questions.explanation: In a stable community the numbers of predators and prey rise and fall in cycles; more prey supports more predators, so the peak in predator numbers follows the peak in prey numbers.

questions.stem: In the carbon cycle, which process removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere?

options.text: Respiration in plants
Decay by microorganisms
Photosynthesis in plants
Burning fossil fuels

questions.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide for photosynthesis; respiration, decay and combustion all release it.

questions.stem: Why must a biogas generator be sealed so that air cannot get in?

options.text: Methane is produced by anaerobic decay
Methane is produced faster in warmer air
Oxygen is needed to produce the methane
Bacteria need air to produce the methane

questions.explanation: Anaerobic decay produces methane gas, so a biogas generator is sealed to keep oxygen out and produce methane gas that can be used as a fuel.

questions.stem: A student places five quadrats at random in a field and counts the daisies in each: 7, 0, 6, 7, 5. What is the mean number of daisies per quadrat?

options.text: 6.0 daisies per quadrat
7.0 daisies per quadrat
5.0 daisies per quadrat
6.25 daisies per quadrat

questions.explanation: The arithmetic mean is the total of the readings divided by the number of readings: 25 daisies divided by 5 quadrats gives 5.0 daisies per quadrat.

questions.stem: Counts of daisies per quadrat range from 2 to 46. Which scale should the student use on the y-axis when plotting these results?

options.text: 0 to 50, using steps of 2, 5, 10
0 to 50, using equal steps of 5
0 to 500, using equal steps of 50
2 to 46, using steps of 4 then 10

questions.explanation: An appropriate scale goes up in equal steps and lets the range of the data fill most of the grid, so all counts from 2 to 46 can be plotted accurately.

questions.stem: Thirty years ago a moss grew across a whole moor. Mean summer temperature has since risen and summer rainfall has fallen, and the moss is now found only in damp hollows. Which conclusion is best supported by this information?

options.text: Human interaction has removed it from this moor
The species is dying out across the whole moor
The plants moved downhill into the damp hollows
The availability of water limits its distribution

questions.explanation: Environmental changes including temperature and availability of water affect the distribution of species, and the moss is now found only where water remains available.
